title: Lesson 41 - The One Next to the Elevator

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Facilities asked for the exact location before they send anyone. Which rail did you mean?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The one next to the elevator, on the wall that faces the service desk.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: There are two rails near the elevator. Do you mean the long one that runs toward the front doors?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: No, the shorter one that ends beside the side-gallery entrance. Its left bracket moves slightly when the empty rail is touched.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: That's the one above the narrow bench, right?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Exactly. The long rail above the brochure table looks secure. I didn't test it; I only compared the brackets visually.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good distinction. We should report what we observed, not diagnose the cause.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Agreed. The place where we noticed the movement is about one meter to the right of the elevator doors.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And no photographs or sample cards were hanging there?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: None. We had already removed our own test materials before we noticed it.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Who handles this kind of request?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The staff member who checked the gallery floor last week gave me a card. I think his name is Sam.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Sam is the facilities coordinator who manages contractor visits. I'll send the report to him, but I want to make the location impossible to confuse.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Add the floor-plan code: Lobby Wall L-2. It's the rail that is next to the elevator and above the narrow bench.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Let me make sure I've got this right. L-2 is the short rail that faces the service desk. The left bracket is the part that moved. The long rail above the brochure table is not the reported one.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: What would you do—close the whole lobby or just keep that rail unused?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: If I were you, I'd ask Sam. The safest option is to keep that rail unused until facilities gives instructions; we don't need to decide the building response ourselves.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: That's sensible. I'll mark only L-2 as unavailable and ask Sam to confirm the next step.
